messages:
maria_sales: Heads up — Acme wants a 2-week Reserved Pool POC. Must provide a single static outbound IP for their external connectors, a dedicated endpoint URL, and ephemeral API keys for their engineers. Can ops confirm what we can commit to and lead times?

ajay_se: We can support. Two approaches: (1) Dedicated endpoint with a single VIP (cleanest for their firewall), or (2) reserve pool nodes NAT'd through 1-3 EIPs for redundancy. VIP is slightly more work but gives them one stable IP/FQDN.

maria_sales: Customer prefers one IP to paste into their allowlist. They also asked for an ops contact and a curl example to smoke test.

nate_netops: For a true single egress IP we can allocate a VIP behind the LB or provide a single EIP and NAT all pool traffic through it. Lead times: EIP reservation ~24h, VIP + DNS ~30-90m after deploy. I need ticket with tag customer:acme-poc + POC window.

maria_sales: Ticket incoming. Are there any restrictions on certs / mTLS?

caroline_cs: Security notes: we log outbound request metadata (timestamp, destination, egress IP) and can export per-request traces for the POC as CSV. TLS is terminated at our edge; if Acme requires mutual TLS to their partners we can present client certs from the nodes — we need destination hostnames and cert acceptance rules. Data retention: POC logs purged after 30 days by default.

nate_netops: Sample allowlist block to give their firewall team (placeholder IPs):
```
# ACME POC - outbound IPs
13.57.99.12/32
44.233.12.77/32
54.210.7.201/32
```

ajay_se: We'll generate a project-scoped API key with TTL=14 days and label it poc-acme. By default keys live in our store; if they later require KMS-backed keys as part of Private, expect +3-5 days for onboarding.

maria_sales: Ryan — can we apply the short-term POC discount on the billing side?

ryan_finance: Yep, mark as internal POC discount and I'll approve. Please include the discount code in the quote.

deploy-bot: reserved-pool created — pool-id: pool-2089, region: us-west-2 (requested by maria_sales)

nate_netops: I've submitted the EIP request. Will post final allocated IP(s) and ticket id here when ready. Also note: if they want to rely on a single IP, we advise using a Security Group rule for TCP/443 from that IP; if they prefer FQDN allowlisting we can provide a stable hostname (acme-poc.rdinfr.dev) but many firewalls expect IPs.

kevin_acme: Thanks — we've opened our firewall change request (ticket ACME-FW-510) referencing the sample IPs. We'll confirm acceptance once our security team signs off.

maria_sales: I'll draft the onboarding email: include allowlist, curl snippet, ops contact, and data retention note.

ajay_se: Curl snippet for their engineers (use POC key placeholder):
```bash
curl -v "https://acme-poc.rdinfr.dev/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_POC_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello world"}'
```

caroline_cs: I'll prepare short bullet answers for their security questionnaire and attach a sample CSV export format for egress traces. Contact for security follow-ups: security@redwood.ai.

nate_netops: Follow-up — EIPs allocated: 13.57.99.12, 44.233.12.77. Ticket NET-4702. Using these as a NAT set will give them two addresses to add; if they strictly need one, we can NAT via the VIP but that requires the dedicated endpoint path.

maria_sales: Great — once Kevin confirms firewall acceptance I'll create the POC key and post creds + curl + final IPs here.

ajay_se: Quick FYI for future: moving from Reserved Pool POC to Private with KMS and VPC peering adds ~3-5 days and some networking prep (peering routes, security audits). Flag that if they ask for production parity.

maria_sales: Thanks team — I'll update the CRM and ping when the handoff email goes out.
